items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy 'what if' geography Short for BHUGOL, a popular geography fun-facts YouTube channel. The Narrator is SUPER excited, practically bursting with energy: a hyped-up, thrilled YouTube host who can't believe how cool this story is and can't wait to tell you. Huge smile in the voice the whole way, bright and punchy, loud-ish and lively. Wide, dramatic pitch movement: rise with real wonder on every question, hit every number with genuine amazement ('WOW' energy), build excitement through each line, and land each punchline with a grin after a tiny comic pause. 'They already did it' gets a playful, knowing, excited lift. 'But that's not even the weirdest part' is whispered-excited, leaning in like a secret. 'a navy!' is said with delighted disbelief. Bolivia's reply 'Keep the capital... just give me the beach!' is a cheeky, chill little voice-wink. The last line trails off unfinished on 'Because honestly...', voice staying up, so it loops straight back into the first line. Pace is quick and bouncy, about 175 words per minute, short crisp pauses; never slow, flat, calm, sleepy, bored or documentary-serious. VOICE IDENTITY: always the same warm baritone host, same person and same high energy level throughout. Accent: native General American English narrator, neutral American accent from the first word to the last. Pronounce Titicaca as tee-tee-KAH-kah, Machu Picchu as MAH-choo PEEK-choo, Lima as LEE-mah, Bolivia as boh-LIV-ee-uh.
lines: Narrator
What if Peru and Bolivia became one country?
Narrator
Sounds crazy? They already did it... in eighteen thirty-six.
Narrator
It was called the Peru-Bolivian Confederation.
Narrator
But the neighbors panicked... and crushed it in just three years.
Narrator
So what would this country get today?
Narrator
Nearly forty-eight million people... and more land than Mexico.
Narrator
The Andes, the Amazon... and Machu Picchu.
Narrator
And Bolivia would finally get back... the ocean.
Narrator
It lost its whole coast to Chile... over a century ago.
Narrator
But that's not even the weirdest part.
Narrator
Landlocked Bolivia still has... a navy!
Narrator
It sails on a lake... Lake Titicaca.
Narrator
And Peru already lent Bolivia a beach... for ninety-nine years!
Narrator
Then there's the capital. Lima? Bolivia already has two!
Narrator
Bolivia's reply? Keep the capital... just give me the beach!
Narrator
So... one country, or two? Because honestly...
